Subject: Pilot activation runbook & validation checklist — Atlas Medical Systems

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposed runbook so we can kick the pilot next week. Short version at the top, then owners and action items.

Call highlights / confirmed pain points:
- High per-call inference cost on your inpatient triage flow (current compute spend is the primary blocker to scaling).
- Inconsistent entity extraction (patient-condition mapping) causing manual review downstream.
- Strict PHI handling and retention policies — you need proof of encrypted at-rest + key control.

Goal for the pilot (success criteria):
- Latency: p95 endpoint latency <= 150ms for 512-token eval workload.
- Quality: entity extraction F1 >= 0.92 on the 30-run prompt suite.
- Cost: 3x reduction in cost-per-inference vs baseline (measured by tokens + GPU time).
- Compliance: demonstrable encryption-at-rest, scoped audit logs, and documented data flow.

Proposed scope (3-week pilot):
Week 0 (access & baseline): VPC peering + SSO + service account; baseline run on 500 sample prompts.
Week 1 (model + prompt tuning): run prompt-set, enable KV caching, iterate model variant and quantization.
Week 2 (validation): full eval suite (30 templates x 100 examples), performance & cost runbook, handoff notes.
Deliverables: pilot-scope-v1.pdf (attached), prompt-set-30.csv (attached), access checklist (attached).

Owners / roles:
- Redwood: Kimberly Park (Engg lead / PM), Ben Carter (Solutions eng), Stephanie Nguyen (Customer success).
- Atlas: Alicia Gomez (Program owner), Samuel Price (Security/infra).

Access checklist (short):
1) SAML SSO metadata for Atlas admin (IDP URL + cert).
2) VPC peering request + CIDR and routing table.
3) S3 location or secure share for redacted sample dataset (we only need de-identified prompts for eval).
4) KMS key policy if you want customer-managed keys.

Immediate asks (please reply with items 1–3 if available):
- Alicia: confirm SSO admin contact and S3 bucket path by EOD Thu.
- Samuel: confirm if Atlas requires HSM-backed keys and your SOC2 contact for evidence requests.
- Atlas: any procurement paperwork we should route to your legal/procurement now? (We can spin up a minimal reserved capacity for the pilot on our end if needed.)

Proposed next step: 30-min activation call to finalize SSO/VPC on Wed, Jun 16 @ 10:00 AM PT. If that works I’ll send the invite and attach the DocuSign link for the pilot order (minimal commitment).

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Thanks Kim — this summary is great and matches what we captured internally. A few quick replies and clarifications: 

- SSO admin: Maria Lopez (mlopez@atlasmed.com) will handle SAML metadata. I’ve looped her on a separate note.
- S3 bucket: s3://atlasmed-pilot/triage-eval (we will populate with de-identified prompts by Tue).
- KMS/HSM: we prefer customer-managed keys for any decrypted output saved by third parties. We can provide a KMS ARN; Samuel owns the key decisions.
- Compliance: our security team will need a short data flow diagram and a SOC2 addendum. Could you send the minimal artifact we can share with legal?

Procurement: we need a short quote for the pilot (3-week) to route to procurement. I also want a short rollback & data-handling clause in the SOW (we’ll ask legal for standard language, but wanted to flag now).

One more ask on evaluation: can you confirm how you’ll measure "cost per inference" so we align on the baseline metrics? Our preferred approach is total GPU runtime + token counts normalized per 1k inference calls — if you have a template we can sign off on it.

Will confirm the 10:00 AM PT window tomorrow after Maria confirms she’s available.

—Alicia
